commits.author: himanshk96
commits.message:
[zephyr] Pickle shuffled items with the stdlib pickler (#9699)

Serialize each shuffled item with the stdlib pickler and read payloads
back
with `pickle.loads`, keeping cloudpickle only as the fallback for items
the
stdlib pickler cannot reference by import path, such as lambdas or
classes
defined inside a function. Every row that crosses a `group_by` was
cloudpickled one item at a time; for the plain dicts and NamedTuples
that
pipelines actually shuffle, the stdlib pickler writes the same stream
several
times faster (0.8 vs 3.0 us for a six-field NamedTuple, 1.3 vs 1.6 us
for a
4 KB document), and both streams decode with `pickle.loads`.

On the decontamination drop-set build, a 3.6M-row shuffle of small
NamedTuples, wall time went from 34.4 and 36.0 s to 31.2 and 30.0 s with
identical payload bytes and an identical drop set. The gain shrinks as
rows
get larger, since the cost becomes the bytes rather than the pickler. A
test
covers the fallback: an item holding a lambda and an instance of a
locally
defined class round-trip through `_items_to_dataframe` and
`_dataframe_to_items`.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[iris] Preserve retry resources during Kubernetes cleanup (#9705)

Delete each obsolete pod’s ConfigMap and PDB by its attempt-specific
name. Cleanup previously selected resources by a task hash shared across
attempts, so it could delete a retry’s ConfigMap before its pod existed.
This caused ten hero tasks to miss startup and the remaining tasks to
wait for a 30-minute JAX registration timeout. Exact-name cleanup
removes the active-task-hash check and keeps failed cleanup queued for
the next pass. Coordinator PDBs are created before their pods so
deleting an old PDB cannot leave a retry unprotected.

Disable W&B source capture in EP and FSDP hero launchers while retaining
git revision metadata. This avoids scanning a changing virtual
environment during tracker initialization, which caused another failed
restart.

The regression test for cleanup racing with retry dispatch fails on the
old code and passes with the fix. All 70 Kubernetes provider tests and
3,163 affected safe tests pass. See the [incident
report](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/592) for the failure timeline.

---------

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[levanter] Expose the pure-JAX flash attention to Grug as xla_flash (#9692)

Grug attention gains an `xla_flash` implementation for AMD GPUs and any
other backend without a CUDA or TPU attention kernel (#9462). It is
Levanter's existing pure-JAX flash attention, which has a custom
backward, called on Grug's raw arrays: KV heads are aligned, the arrays
named, and Grug's causal, sliding-window and segment-id mask translated
into Levanter's. The module moves from `levanter.models` to
`levanter.layers`, beside the attention module that was its only caller,
so the Grug layer can import it without reaching above itself. The block
size is the largest power of two that divides both sequence lengths,
capped at 1024, with the reference path for lengths no block of at least
16 divides. The wrapper lives in `levanter.grug.attention._xla_flash`.
The Snowball synthetic harness gains an `--attention` flag that accepts
every Grug attention implementation.

A scan-based blockwise draft without a custom backward was measured
first on 8× MI300X with the 4-layer Snowball shape and was slower than
the reference at both 4,096 and 16,384 tokens, and used more memory at
16,384 (1.38 s against 0.935 s per step, 92 against 81 GiB), because
autodiff stored every key block for the backward pass. That is why the
existing implementation is reused rather than a new one added. Measured
the same way, `xla_flash` runs within 4% of the reference step time at
both lengths (0.395 against 0.385 s at 4,096 tokens, 0.968 against 0.935
s at 16,384) and cuts peak memory from 81 to 32 GiB per GPU at 16,384
tokens, with identical loss.

Part of #9462

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[CatCountCanary] Offer dry and gate presets with optional export (#9643)

CatCount offers a one-step dry preset and a gate preset that stops when
sampled training reward reaches 0.65, with a cap of 30 steps. Both use
two update epochs; asynchronous rollouts allow two steps of staleness.

The default gate run has no checkpoint or Hugging Face export callbacks.
Explicit export enables both callbacks and a positive checkpoint
interval, with the result preserved through the existing round trip.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Port verifyit grading logic and tests into Marin

Import the grading logic and tests developed in [verifyit](https://github.com/marin-community/verifyit) into `lib/verifyit` in the Marin workspace. Include the verifier-unification core from [#6](https://github.com/marin-community/verifyit/pull/6) at [`c3914da`](https://github.com/marin-community/verifyit/commit/c3914da8ebe46011da7239d3c9ecdfc5fb4c54da), the in-memory judge and Reasoning Gym APIs from [#2](https://github.com/marin-community/verifyit/pull/2) and [#5](https://github.com/marin-community/verifyit/pull/5), and the shell-output and strict JSON comparators from [#7](https://github.com/marin-community/verifyit/pull/7) and [#8](https://github.com/marin-community/verifyit/pull/8).

The port adds grading of extracted candidate values, explicit empty-answer policies, bounded execution and artifact reads, shared aggregation and normalization, and opt-in adapters for SkyRL, Harbor, Evalchemy, and lm-eval-harness. Invalid tasks and infrastructure failures discard partial credit; pytest collection failures are now infrastructure errors. The package rename, current consumer updates, and CI registration are in prerequisite #9698. Verifyit's standalone CI workflows, contributor skills, and marin-style setup are excluded. Dependency and lockfile updates support the imported logic.

The verifier suite passed 1,231 tests with two skips, the safe Marin suite passed 2,386 tests with four skips and five expected failures, and TaskCompendium passed 74 tests. Focused tests covering advisory cleanup, formatting, lint, type checking, and wheel/source builds passed.

Supersedes the closed spin-out migration [#9567](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9567). The adapter implementations are included; adoption in external SkyRL, Harbor, Evalchemy, and lm-eval-harness repositories remains separate.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[deps] Match the pipeline FA4 stack to Levanter's GPU pins (#9353)

The root pipeline extra still allowed flash-attn-4 4.0.0b16, CUTLASS DSL
4.6.0 and QuACK 0.6.1, while levanter[gpu] requires flash-attn-4
>=4.0.0b27, CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2 and QuACK 0.6.4, and Marin's FA4 adapters
call the newer preprocess and postprocess signatures. Use Levanter's
pins in the pipeline extra; the lock resolves flash-attn-4 to 4.0.0b28.
JAX stays at 0.11.0 for JaxPP.

With these pins, FA4's unpinned Torch import resolves standalone
levanter[gpu] installs to a CUDA Torch 2.10.0 from PyPI. A flat
CPU-Torch fallback index keeps those installs on CPU Torch;
marin-core[gpu] still selects its CUDA Torch index explicitly.

The same versions (flash-attn-4 4.0.0b28, CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2, QuACK
0.6.4, JAX 0.11.0) have run under JaxPP on H100 in the context-parallel
integration (#9283, results in #9277): an eight-layer PP4/EP4/CP2
pipeline completed ten updates on 32 H100s, and the full 535B model
completed ten updates on 192 H100s. Those runs also used scratch JaxPP
overlays, and the environment built from this lock has not itself been
run on GPU.

commits.author: himanshk96
commits.message:
[datakit] Cut Python work in the decontamination mark pass (#9690)

Check for an alphabetic character with `any(map(str.isalpha, ngram))`,
split
each paragraph once for both the short-exact feature and the n-gram
extraction, and read only the `id` and text columns in the mark pass
instead
of every metadata column normalize preserved. The same alpha check
replaces
the per-character loops on the streaming path for texts above 1 MiB,
blake2b
is bound once for `_bloom_hash`, and the bloom filter is loaded through
a
node-local copy shared by every process on the worker instead of being
read
from object storage once per shard (162,535 reads of a 270 MB filter in
the
last production run); bloom dirs are content-addressed step outputs, so
a path
identifies its contents. The mark pass is the one decontamination stage
that scans every
document, and a profile on this hardware put about 90% of its time in
Python
string work rather than bloom probes.

Outputs are byte-identical. A differential run of the previous and new
module
over 47 documents covering blank-line and single-newline paragraphs,
digit-only text, short exact matches, NBSP and U+001C-U+001F separators,
combining marks, empty and null text, a paragraph above the 1 MiB
streaming
threshold, and drop sets produced identical attributes, flagged samples,
bloom
index and drop sets; the alphabetic check was compared on every Unicode
codepoint, the paragraph overlap fuzzed on 15,000 random paragraphs, and
the
streaming path checked on 1 MiB texts with 2, 3, 12 and 13 huge tokens.
A
parquet without the text column still scores every document clean, as
before.
With the first three edits, on 102,602 documents with the production
eval
bloom and drop sets on eight workers, the mark pass went from 112 s to
91 s
with identical output files, and the mark core from 0.90 to 0.67 us per
13-gram. The remaining cost is blake2b plus split and join; moving the
feature
extraction into dupekit is the next step.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[fray] Add MI355X peak FLOPs (#9688)

Add an mi355x entry to the device FLOPs table and map JAX's "AMD
Instinct MI355X" device kind to it. Before this, MFU lookups on MI355X
returned no peak, because the name does not contain "mi350x".

MI355X is the MI350X die (gfx950) at a higher clock and power limit. The
values are the dense peaks from [AMD's MI355X
datasheet](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/instinct-tech-docs/product-briefs/amd-instinct-mi355x-gpu-brochure.pdf):
2.5166 PFLOP/s fp16/bf16, 5.0332 PFLOP/s OCP-FP8 and int8, 157.3 TFLOP/s
fp32 matrix, 78.6 TFLOP/s fp64 matrix.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[levanter] Record the launch commit and dirty state in W&B (#9637)

W&B runs from the canary ferries and the hero have an empty
`git_commit`. `WandbConfig` looked up the commit only after checking
that the source directory fit the 20 MB code-capture limit, and returned
early when it did not. The tracked Marin checkout is about 65 MB, so the
lookup never ran. The commit is now looked up whether or not the source
is captured, including with `save_code=False`, and a failed lookup logs
its error.

An Iris task runs from a bundle without `.git`, so a local lookup finds
nothing there. Iris already passes each job the submitter's git
provenance in `MARIN_PROVENANCE` (#7000). When `GIT_COMMIT` and a local
checkout give no commit, `WandbConfig` now uses the provenance's short
`base_commit`. It also records the provenance's `git_dirty` flag and
`git_tree_hash` in the run config, so a run launched from a checkout
with uncommitted changes is marked. The tree hash covers tracked files,
including their uncommitted edits. Untracked files set the dirty flag
but do not change the hash, although the Iris bundle ships the ones that
are not ignored, so two dirty launches can report the same hash with
different bundled source. A run outside Iris has no `MARIN_PROVENANCE`,
so its provenance is captured from the same checkout the commit is read
from, which can differ from the working directory. The dirty flag and
tree hash are dropped when the provenance names a different commit from
the one recorded. The full provenance also holds the submitter's
username, command line, and remote URL; those are left out of the W&B
config, which may be public.

Canary runs get their commit this way with no workflow change. Their
`git_commit` is the short hash, so joins against full SHAs need a prefix
match. The first scheduled canary after this merges will show whether
the GitHub runner's checkout reports as clean.

Updates `urllib3` from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0


Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's
releases.




2.8.0


🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support


urllib3
is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure
long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or
organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in
Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing
financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and
maintained for the long-haul.


Thank you for your support.


Security


Fixed the following security issues:


    

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or
overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
    • 

  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked()
could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High
severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
    • 

  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium
severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)
    • 





[!IMPORTANT]
urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or
overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that
behavior may require changes.


Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in
proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with
proxy_assert_hostname or
proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates
and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy
connections.






[!NOTE]
CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of
release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.




Deprecations & Removals


    

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry
option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)
    • 



Features


    

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and
Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the
result of parse_url(). (#4945)
    • 

  • Added basic_auth_encoding and
proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to
urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)
    • 



Bugfixes


    

  • 

    Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header
lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112,
preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as
Set-Cookie. (#1362)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with
ProxyManager when
use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing
ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for
HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a
FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)
    

    • 

  • 

    Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool
initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the
queue module after the ConnectionPool is
instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls
class property. This is done because sometimes the
queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such
as by gevent. (#3289)
    

    • 

  • 

    Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of
ValueError when retrying a request whose body had
tell() but not seek(). (#3779)
    

    • 

  • 

    Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating
with the proxy server. (#3785)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread
response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt
when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms
accepted by socket.connect, such as hex
(0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal
integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate
verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading
FullPoolError instead of ValueError when
called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created
with block=True. (#5059)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values
instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool
selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and
HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071,
#5101)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the
assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint
parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy
forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before
sending requests. (#5079)
    

    • 

  • 

    Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential
security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and
HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and
Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on
newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the
same security fixes. (#5091)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding
ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy
identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when
forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.
    

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI,
assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and
continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an
HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax,
rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters,
malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in
HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel
targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization
rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved
characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained
percent-encoded octets. (#5095)
    

    •

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[evaldash] Show grades for MRCR samples (#9509)

MRCR reports `mrcr_accuracy` for the run but records `accuracy` on each
example. Marin's Evalchemy sample exporter required the aggregate name,
so the [September 27 Grug
run](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20260927-131914-open-athena-Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21-mrcr-13d8)
shows 1,196 of 1,196 items graded in its summary and 1,196 ungraded
samples in its inspector. A sample carries `accuracy: 0.0486` and
`prefix_hit: 1` with no grading object.

Map the aggregate metric to the sample metric during export. For
existing archives, EvalDash derives the displayed grade and correctness
from the recorded `accuracy` without rewriting stored data. This should
make the run's incorrect filter usable after deployment without
rerunning MRCR.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
Add RL Data Atlas quality reviews and difficulty evidence (#9518)

Add the RL Data Atlas applet for browsing MarinSkyRL and Task Trove
sources with filtered task totals, source provenance, and linked quality
reviews. Catalog refresh detects dataset or verifier changes and marks
affected reviews stale. Review pages retain historical audits and
supplemental findings, highlight technical issues, and distinguish
inspected code from native execution. Source-bound verifier revision
reviews appear alongside the original solver and judge results.
Confirmed verifier defects cap Quality at Some issues, retain existing
Bad ratings, and prevent current difficulty measurements until native
checks validate the fix and a new source review covers the current data
and verifier revisions.

Replace Difficulty prose with model solve-rate bars and numeric sorting.
Each comparison links to collapsible model identities, applied settings,
saved requests and responses, and native verifier outputs. Current v3
comparisons require fixed Qwen3 Coder 30B, Qwen3.5 122B, and hosted
GLM-5.3 identities with a shared 65,536-token context and 16,384-token
output budget. The Large model uses nonthinking decoding with top-p 0.8
and presence penalty 1.5; the app validates these settings before
counting a measurement as current. Earlier comparisons display their
actual model names and Historical status. Table cells use short model
labels and percentages. An ordering warning appears as an icon there;
the review page shows its full explanation and solve counts. TaskTrove
science uses a recorded Qwen3.5-9B verifier judge with thinking
disabled. Three checklist sources use a separate recorded
DeepSeek-V4-Pro verifier judge through Together because the original
GPT-4o-mini credential has exhausted credits. Both judge protocols
retain the same three solver models and token budgets. Filters and
sorting use only current Qwen3.5 122B results. Preserve earlier reports
and verifier rerun outputs with their original execution logs. Evidence
loads when its section opens.

Authenticate Hugging Face metadata requests through HF_TOKEN_READONLY
version 1, matching the scoped Marina grant in #9501. Send review
uploads through standard input to avoid macOS command-argument size
limits.

The [legacy GLM serving incident
record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/554) preserves the failed
weight-load and cleanup timeline, immutable evidence, and unverified
HTTP 404 attempts. Earlier completed difficulty comparisons predate that
outage; the storage read cause remains unresolved.

Publish the Atlas at its stable [public
URL](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/fb11c931-5861-4878-8bb5-a964d652b45f/).
Public visitors browse the saved catalog without signing in;
authenticated visits still trigger upstream refreshes.

The [Atlas Small serving incident
record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/557) documents the 24-hour
endpoint expiry, three unverified Harbor attempts, failed RunAI S3
streaming reloads, and recovery with the same pinned model staged on the
worker. The infrastructure-failed attempts are preserved for replay
before their source's difficulty is published.

The [staged Qwen serving incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/560)
records the later RNO2A preemption failures, preservation of proxy-error
attempts, and recovery on US-EAST-02A with unchanged model settings.

The [US-EAST-02A Iris endpoint-proxy
incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/561) records completion stalls
despite healthy vLLM pods and the Kubernetes pod-proxy mitigation.

The [wrong-checkout applet
incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/562) records the brief
revision 43 regression, rollback to revision 42, and recovery with the
reviewed package at revision 45.

Fixes #9499

commits.message:
[rl-mismatch] Launch probes and report comparison metrics (#9506)

Launch a frozen-token RL mismatch probe through Marin's existing SkyRL
artifact graph. The Iceball preset configures the probe in Iceball's
recipe through `iceball_rl_spec` and `iceball_rl_execution`, takes model
and data artifact roots, and accepts an update count, a warm checkpoint
and a reusable archive. Probe updates start at zero while the resumed
trainer retains its absolute step and optimizer state. Temporary
checkpoints and attempts use 30-day storage; probe archives remain in
the durable run artifact.

Render FineStore archives as JSON, Markdown and route-agreement plots on
CPU. Typed report records describe token identity, masked
log-probability comparisons, importance-ratio statistics, paired
prompt-cluster bootstrap intervals for differences between routing
modes, and sampling-distribution checks. Complete archives require
native trainer scores and sampler generation scores. Cross-run
comparisons check the starting checkpoint path, step and MarinSkyRL
runtime commit, alongside token, tokenizer, sampling and cache settings.
Reports identify the archive snapshot read and include scoring timings
with worker dispatch and compilation.

[An Iceball zero-update
launch](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-mismatch-probe-iceball-micro-rl-2026.10.01.17-coordinator-da5c44e0)
validates recipe composition and probe startup.
